scope: Curated trace of the available conversation; paraphrases, not verbatim quotations. This inquiry provenance graph is not an implementation of the proposed reasoning-object substrate. Updated through the standards-mapping authorization. No unmerged implementation is incorporated.

statusDefinitions.accepted: Explicit user request, correction, or approval.
statusDefinitions.accepted_direction: Assistant clarification consistent with subsequent user direction; exact mechanism not separately approved.
statusDefinitions.proposed: Assistant mechanism awaiting specification or review.

nodes.title: Worlds and candidate values belong with sentence structure

evidence.text: User rejected the world being absent from 'the world decides' and asked for sentence and suppositional candidates as one thing.

nodes.title: Retain all worlds and suppositions within declared scope

evidence.text: User wanted all suppositions and worlds in one object, acknowledging that complete displays may become intractable.

nodes.title: Provide coordinated partial views

evidence.text: User requested viewing subsections of the larger object.

nodes.title: Use simple examples and demanding families

evidence.text: User requested initial demonstrations and complex examples to test extensibility and formalization; finite examples alone cannot prove generality.

nodes.title: Detached or multiplexed tables are insufficient as the main notation

evidence.text: User said the displayed chart felt like standard symbolic representation rather than schematic dynamic machinery.

nodes.title: Connected machinery and visible exploration

evidence.text: User proposed pathways and electronic-circuit-like structure including sentences, worlds, and the process of playing out possibilities.

nodes.title: Worlds are not permanently inputs

evidence.text: User suggested a statement's truth could select a set of worlds; assistant revised one-way input framing to joint constraints.

nodes.title: Suppositions, propagation, entailment, and branching differ

evidence.text: User asked how supposing and its entailments fit; assistant distinguished temporary restrictions, local consequences, global entailment, and alternative trials.

nodes.title: Infinity-groupoid and ruliad

evidence.text: User offered these terms tentatively. Assistant identified fixed-rule multiway histories as a closer analogy and explained why reversibility and universal computation were not adopted.

nodes.title: Prioritize precise shared objects and inspectable reasoning

evidence.text: User explicitly agreed with the goals and priorities, then asked whether review concerned human cognition or formal computation.

nodes.title: Separate formal correctness from human intelligibility

evidence.text: Assistant corrected the conflation: machine checks and proof obligations are separate from Brian's visual review.

nodes.title: Machine-checkable substrate with potentially intractable instances

evidence.text: User requested formal computationally checkable structure, compact visual explanations of liar/loops/halting, and views relevant to a question.

nodes.title: Question-directed view contracts

evidence.text: Assistant distinguished restriction, projection, collapse, and abstraction; warned that selecting a useful exact view may itself be difficult.

nodes.title: An object is broader than a sentence

evidence.text: User clarified that an instance may involve sentences, worlds, facts, suppositional pathways, and true/false values. Assistant adopted typed structured reasoning objects.

nodes.title: Align repository and preserve inquiry trace

evidence.text: User requested making the repository consistent with this direction and updating the inquiry graph trace.

nodes.title: Specify executable schema and rule verification

evidence.text: No general typed schema or context-aware inference checker is implemented by this documentation revision.

nodes.title: Review a connected schematic

evidence.text: No new gate or pathway notation has been visually approved.

nodes.title: Prove view guarantees within declared scope

evidence.text: Projection must preserve dependencies and supporting extensions; approximate summaries require explicit guarantees.

nodes.title: Formalize richer self-reference and program behavior

evidence.text: Strange loops require precise examples; arithmetic and halting need encodings and assumptions beyond predicate labels.

nodes.title: Merge contract and prepare executable snow-object review

evidence.text: After the assistant proposed merging PR #4 and preparing a checked snow object and schematic, the user approved. The approval did not approve unseen graphical marks.

nodes.title: Explain world cases and introduce one piece at a time

evidence.text: The user did not understand the world-fact T/F-open label, asked whether it covered relevant worlds, and requested a gradual tutorial. The assistant supplied a 15-stage conversational walkthrough.

nodes.title: Recover the inventory of primitives

evidence.text: The user asked for the ontological primitives after losing track. The assistant gave a component inventory that insufficiently distinguished mathematical levels.

nodes.title: Separate entities, names, references, and entailments

evidence.text: The user questioned missing ordinary entities, the meaning of reference, and whether inference records were entailments. The assistant clarified denotation and proof/consequence distinctions.

nodes.title: Use existing formalizations instead of inventing elementary logic

evidence.text: The user challenged the plausibility of creating these foundations ourselves. The assistant acknowledged that the basic distinctions and much graphical logic are already established.

nodes.title: Research the mapping and select a foundation

evidence.text: The user authorized mapping project components to established definitions and comparing foundations before further custom primitives.

nodes.title: Compose model theory, finite constraints, established proofs, and relational views

evidence.text: Research recommendation: use existing mathematical structures and prove the project's translations. The exact implementation and final graphical notation remain reviewable choices.

nodes.title: Validate translations into established frameworks

evidence.text: Compile supported syntax to constraints with a correspondence argument, connect proof records to a named calculus, and state each view's preservation contract. Existing formalizations do not certify unverified application code.
